extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies and owners/operators of affected electric generating units (EGUs)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements for monitoring, calculating, reporting, recordkeeping, submission, and definitions to demonstrate compliance with EPA CO2 emissions standards for affected electric generating units and State plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of P_gross/net (units and conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate P_gross/net for your affected EGU (or group of affected EGUs that share a monitored common stack) using the specified equation. All terms must be expressed in units of MWh. To convert each hourly gross or net energy output value reported under 40 CFR part 75 to MWh, multiply by the corresponding EGU or stack operating time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines P_GROSS/NET as gross or net energy output for each valid operating hour (as defined in 60.5860b(a)(2)) in MWh. Lists constituent terms (PE_ST, PE_CT, PE_IE, PE_A, PT_PS, PT_HR, PT_IE) and requires unit consistency; includes TDF factor rules for CHP (0.95 or 1.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of PE_ST, PE_CT, PE_IE, PE_A, PT_PS, PT_HR, PT_IE
rubrics_metrics.description: PE_ST = electric plus mechanical energy output of steam turbines; PE_CT = electric plus mechanical output of stationary combustion turbines; PE_IE = electric/mechanical output from integrated equipment; PE_A = electric energy used for auxiliary loads; PT_PS = useful thermal output of steam used for non-electric applications; PT_HR = non-steam useful thermal output from heat recovery; PT_IE = useful thermal output from integrated equipment used for non-steam/electric applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All energy outputs must be expressed in MWh and measured relative to SATP conditions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: TDF (transmission and distribution factor) application
rubrics_metrics.description: TDF = 0.95 for a combined heat and power affected EGU where at least annually 20.0% of total gross or net energy output is electric/direct mechanical and 20.0% is useful thermal on a 12-operating month rolling average basis, or 1.0 for all other affected EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 0.95 divisor to the electric portion for qualifying CHP facilities per gross/net output definitions in the equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of Pt_PS for CHP (Equation 2 inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable (e.g., combined heat and power), calculate (Pt)PS using Q_M (measured steam flow in kg or lbs), H (enthalpy at measured temperature/pressure relative to SATP or condensate energy), and CF (conversion factor 3.6×10^9 J/MWh or 3.413×10^6 BTU/MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured hourly steam flow and enthalpy and apply the conversion factor to produce MWh of thermal output for Pt_PS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based CO2 emissions rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, sum all P_gross/net values for valid operating hours; divide the total CO2 mass emissions for the valid operating hours by the sum of P_gross/net values to determine CO2 emissions rate (lb/gross or net MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency in the set of valid operating hours and units (MWh and lb). Use CO2 mass emissions from the applicable monitoring provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common stack monitoring option (§60.13(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs share a common exhaust gas stack and are subject to the same emissions standard, the owner/operator may monitor hourly CO2 mass emissions at the common stack instead of monitoring each EGU separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chosen, the hourly gross or net electric output for the common stack must be the sum of hourly outputs of the individual affected EGUs and operating time must be expressed as 'stack operating hours' per 40 CFR 72.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple stacks/ducts monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If exhaust gases are emitted through multiple stacks (or routed to a common stack through multiple ducts and monitoring in the ducts is elected), hourly CO2 mass emissions and 'stack operating time' at each stack or duct must be monitored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine compliance by summing CO2 mass emissions measured at individual stacks/ducts and dividing by the gross or net energy output for the affected EGU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment when EGUs serve common generator
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more affected EGUs serve a common electric generator, apportion the combined hourly gross or net energy output to the individual EGUs according to the fraction of the total steam load contributed by each EGU, or if the EGUs are identical, apportion according to fraction of total heat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use steam load fractions or heat input fractions (for identical units) to allocate generation for compliance calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly fuel usage reporting by owners/operators (affected EGUs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must measure and report monthly fuel usage for each affected source subject to standards with: (i) calendar month of use; (ii) each type of fuel used that month; and (iii) quantity of each fuel combusted with units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete monthly fuel type and quantity detail for each compliance period month.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan record retention minimum (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must require owners/operators of each affected EGU to maintain records for at least 5 years following the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the minimum retention period required of State plans for records relevant to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site record availability requirement (2 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must maintain each record on site for at least 2 years after the date of each occurrence, measurement, maintenance, corrective action, report, or record, whichever is latest, per §60.7. Off-site electronic maintenance is allowed for the remaining years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records may be stored off-site electronically after the 2-year on-site period but must be retrievable for expeditious review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records required to be kept in accessible form
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must keep documents, data files, calculations and methods used to demonstrate compliance; copies of all reports submitted to the State; and data required to be recorded by 40 CFR part 75 subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review by agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports must include all hourly CO2 emissions per affected EGU
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must include in reports all hourly CO2 emissions for each affected EGU (or group of EGUs sharing a monitored common stack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hourly CO2 emissions must be reported for every valid operating hour as specified by monitoring provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based standard report contents (hourly details)
rubrics_metrics.description: For rate-based standards, each report must include: (i) hourly CO2 mass emission rate values (tons/hr) and unit (or stack) operating times for each valid operating hour; (ii) gross or net electric output and P_gross/net for each valid hour; (iii) calculated CO2 mass emissions (lb) per valid hour; (iv) sums of hourly gross/net energy output and hourly CO2 mass emissions for all valid hours; and (v) the calculated CO2 mass emission rate (lbs/gross or net MWh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report values as monitored under part 75; ensure units are consistent and sums reconcile to hourly values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report must include applicable standard and demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each affected EGU report must include the applicable standard of performance and a demonstration that it met the standard; include the EGU's calculated emission performance as a CO2 emission rate in units of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit linkage between measured/calculated performance and the standard metric used in the State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow additional State plan MRR requirements (§60.5740b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must follow any additional monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements in a State plan required under §60.5740b if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-specific provisions may add or modify federal baseline MRR requirements; compliance must incorporate those.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting captured CO2 (part 98 subparts)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU captures CO2 to meet the standard, the owner/operator must report per 40 CFR part 98 subpart PP and either (1) part 98 subpart RR or VV if injection occurs on-site; (2) transfer to a facility reporting under subpart RR or VV if injection off-site; or (3) transfer to a facility with an innovative technology waiver from EPA per paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate reporting path for captured CO2 depending on injection location or waived arrangements; follow subpart-specific reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of captured CO2 transfer requirement (demonstration standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request EPA waiver of transfer requirement if they demonstrate technology will store captured CO2 as effectively as geologic sequestration and will not cause unreasonable risk to public health/welfare/safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will consider operating history, whether technology increases other pollutant emissions, permanence of storage; may require testing, condition approval on monitoring/reporting, withdraw approval on evidence of releases, and will provide public notice of requests and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping of State plan component support materials (§60.5865b(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of all information relied upon in support of any demonstration of State plan components, State plan requirements, supporting documentation, and status of meeting State plan requirements defined in the State plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive support materials used to justify or document State plan elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep records of data submitted by owners/operators used to determine compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: States must keep records of all data submitted by owners/operators that are used to determine compliance with each affected EGU emissions standard or State plan requirement, consistent with requirements in §60.5860b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gaps between submission and State retention of the underlying data used for compliance assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions under 40 CFR part 75 may satisfy State recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State requires hourly CO2 emissions and gross generation or heat input info to calculate compliance and owners/operators submit that data electronically to EPA under 40 CFR part 75, that submission meets the State's recordkeeping requirement; the State is not required to keep duplicate records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary duplication where federal electronic reporting already provides required data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten-year record retention for compliance-determining records
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records for a minimum of 10 years from the date the record is used to determine compliance with an emissions standard or State plan requirement. Each record must be in a form suitable and readily available for expeditious review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a longer-term retention requirement distinct from the 5-year State-plan-specific minimum; ensure records tied to compliance decisions are retained for the full 10-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for compliance date extension provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If State plan includes compliance date extension provisions (§60.5740b(a)(11)), keep records of information required in §60.5740b(a)(11)(i) from affected EGUs that use the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document extension justifications and supporting materials as specified in the referenced provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for short-term reliability mechanism provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If State plan includes a short-term reliability mechanism (§60.5740b(a)(12)), keep records of the information required in §60.5740b(a)(12)(iii) from affected EGUs using that mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain documentation of events and actions taken under short-term reliability provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for reliability assurance mechanism provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If State plan includes a reliability assurance mechanism (§60.5740b(a)(13)), keep records of information required in §60.5740b(a)(13)(vi) from EGUs that use the mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain evidence and metrics used to support reliability assurance actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report timing and method (§60.5870b)
rubrics_metrics.description: States must submit an annual report to EPA including specified information for each calendar year reporting period; reports must be submitted by March 1 of the following year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the annual March 1 deadline for each reporting year; include the full set of required contents in paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: emissions performance and compliance status
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report must include the emissions performance achieved by each affected EGU during the reporting period and identification of whether each EGU is in compliance with its standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-EGU performance metrics and explicit compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: comparison of standard vs actual
rubrics_metrics.description: Include, for each affected EGU, a comparison of the CO2 standard of performance in the State plan versus the actual CO2 emission performance achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show numeric comparisons and any variances or exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: sums of emissions, gross output, and heat input by fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Include, for each affected EGU, the sum of the CO2 emissions, the sum of the gross energy output, and the sum of the heat input for each fuel type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out totals by fuel type for clarity and verification of fuel-specific metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report enforcement actions initiated against affected EGUs during the reporting period under any State plan standard of performance or compliance schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and describe enforcement actions, dates, and outcomes or statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: increments of progress and facility status
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify achievement of any increment of progress required by the State plan and identify designated facilities that have ceased operation during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document milestones and facility retirements relevant to the State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: emission inventory for new designated facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit emission inventory data for designated facilities that were not in operation at State plan development but began operation during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include newly operating facilities' inventory data to keep State plan information current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report content: additional and technical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit additional data as necessary to update prior submissions, and submit copies of technical reports on all performance testing on designated facilities, complete with concurrently recorded process data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure technical testing reports include raw/process data to support test results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan and supporting material submission via SPeCS/CDX
rubrics_metrics.description: All State plan submittals, supporting materials, plan revisions, and State reports required to be submitted to EPA must be reported through EPA's SPeCS, accessible at EPA's Central Data Exchange (CDX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the web-accessible SPeCS/CDX system for official electronic submittals; CBI must be submitted separately via physical media as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBI submission procedure for State plan materials
rubrics_metrics.description: States claiming CBI for submittals or supporting documentation must submit that information on compact disc, flash drive, or other commonly used electronic storage media to U.S. EPA/OAQPS/CORE CBI Office at the specified postal address, clearly marked as CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the mailing instructions and address precisely; electronically-submitted CBI options are also described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized official requirement for official submittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a submittal by the Governor or the Governor's designee by an electronic submission through SPeCS is considered an official submittal to EPA under this subpart. If a different responsible official is designated, EPA must be notified via letter from the Governor prior to the May 11, 2026 deadline (or provide previous delegation documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters must identify designee name/contact and State plan preparers who need SPeCS access; preparer names may be submitted earlier to expedite access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-editable and editable format submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be in a non-editable format; all State plan components designated as federally enforceable must also be submitted in an editable version. Following initial approval, States must provide editable copies of any revision to federally enforceable components and indicate changes (e.g., redline/strikethrough).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editable copies must show changes; submitted changes are not part of the State plan until EPA formally approves them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide both non-editable and editable copies for revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: States must provide the EPA non-editable and editable copies of any submitted revision to existing approved federally enforceable State plan components; editable copies must indicate State-level changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the editable version clearly marks proposed changes; EPA approval is required to incorporate changes into the State plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/reporting for EGUs committing to permanent cessation by 1/1/2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of EGUs that committed to permanently cease operations by Jan 1, 2032 must maintain records and submit reports as listed, including initial, annual status, and final reports per the electronic reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific timelines and content requirements apply, including an initial report 5 years before planned cessation or by State plan submission date, annual progress reports thereafter, and a final report within 6 months after closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial permanent cessation report content (5 years prior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial report must include: (i) a summary of process steps required for permanent cessation including timing, duration, and notification requirements (e.g., notice to reliability authority, retirement filings); and (ii) supporting regulatory documents such as correspondence/official filings with RTO/ISO/PUC, deactivation-related reliability assessments, SEC filings, integrated resource plans/PUC orders, reliability analyses, notifications about reliability needs, and altered deactivation timing notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive supporting regulatory documents (items A–G) to substantiate the planned permanent cessation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual status reports for permanent cessation period
rubrics_metrics.description: For each remaining year prior to committed cessation, submit an annual status report including progress on each identified process step from the initial report and supporting regulatory documents demonstrating progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and provide filings/correspondence with relevant authorities to evidence progress toward deactivation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final permanent cessation report within 6 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a final report no later than 6 months following the committed closure date documenting actions taken after ceasing operation to ensure cessation is permanent, including regulatory filings or decommissioning plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of decommissioning steps and filings that demonstrate permanence of cessation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent Cessation reporting method (CEDRI/CDX) and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning Nov 12, 2024, Permanent Cessation reports must be submitted in PDF format via CEDRI accessed through EPA's CDX. Information submitted through CEDRI will be made public without further notice; do not use CEDRI to submit CBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserting CBI, follow the separate CBI submission procedures; items not marked as CBI may be publicly released.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBI claims and emissions data non-confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: To assert CBI, submit a complete file including claimed CBI to EPA CBI office with clear markings; information not marked as CBI may be released. Under CAA section 114(c), emissions data is not entitled to confidential treatment and will be made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All CBI claims must be asserted at time of submission; anything submitted via CEDRI cannot later be claimed CBI. Submit the same file to CDX with CBI omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred electronic method and contact for CBI submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method to receive CBI is electronically via email attachments, FTP, or file-sharing services transmitted to OAQPS CBI Office at oaqpscbi@epa.gov; for large files request a file transfer link via that email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear CBI markings and flag to the attention of the Emission Guidelines Sector Lead when emailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing option and handling for CBI
rubrics_metrics.description: If electronic transmission is not possible, send CBI via postal service to U.S. EPA Attn: OAQPS Document Control Officer at the specified RTP NC address. Mailed CBI should be double wrapped, clearly marked, and markings should not show through the outer envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address mailed materials to the Greenhouse Gas Emissions for Electric Utility Generating Units Sector Lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic maintenance of records submitted via CEDRI
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required to be maintained that are submitted electronically via CEDRI may be maintained in electronic format, but this does not affect the requirement to make records, data, and reports available upon request to delegated agencies or EPA for on-site compliance evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain electronic records in accessible formats and be prepared to provide them during inspections or reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA system outage claim procedure (CEDRI/CDX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may assert a claim of EPA system outage for failure to timely comply with electronic submission requirements if they meet criteria: outage precluded access within five business days prior to due date; outage may be planned/unplanned; must notify Administrator in writing as soon as possible; must provide dates/times of unavailability, rationale attributing delay to outage, measures taken to minimize delay, and proposed reporting date or actual report date; acceptance is at Administrator's discretion; report must be submitted as soon as possible after outage resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document access attempts, outage timeframe, and mitigation steps; Administrator has sole discretion to accept the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force majeure claim procedure for electronic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may assert force majeure if an event beyond control prevents timely electronic submission within five business days prior to due date; must notify Administrator in writing ASAP; provide written description of event, rationale attributing delay to event, measures to minimize delay, and proposed reporting date or actual report date; decision to accept claim and allow extension is at Administrator's discretion; reporting must occur as soon as possible after event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include natural disasters, acts of war/terrorism, equipment failure; document causal link and mitigation measures thoroughly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator approval required for alternatives to electronic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any alternatives to electronic reporting required by this subpart must be approved by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not unilaterally substitute alternative reporting mechanisms without express EPA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Affected electric generating unit (Affected EGU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGU means a steam generating unit that meets the relevant applicability conditions in §60.5845b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to applicability conditions for scope determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Annual capacity factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual capacity factor means the ratio between actual heat input to an EGU during a calendar year and the potential heat input had it been operated for 8,760 hours at base load rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify utilization relative to maximum steady-state capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Base load rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Base load rating means the maximum amount of heat input an EGU can combust on a steady-state basis as determined by physical design and characteristics at ISO conditions; for turbines/IGCC it includes duct burner heat input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base load rating is used as the denominator for annual capacity factor calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Coal-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired means an electric utility steam generating or IGCC unit that burns coal for >10.0% of average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or >15.0% of annual heat input during any one calendar year after Dec 31, 2029, or retains capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thresholds determine classification and potential applicability of specific standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined cycle unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined cycle unit means a stationary combustion turbine whose exhaust heat is recovered by an HRSG to generate additional electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize combined cycle configurations for applicable calculation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Combined heat and power (CHP) unit
rubrics_metrics.description: CHP (cogeneration) means an electric generating unit that uses a steam-generating unit or stationary combustion turbine to simultaneously produce electric (or mechanical) and useful thermal output from the same primary energy source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHP-specific energy accounting (gross/net definitions and TDF) applies to units meeting CHP criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance period means an annual (calendar year) period for an affected EGU to comply with a standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calendar year reporting for compliance evaluation unless State plan specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Derate
rubrics_metrics.description: Derate means a decrease in available capacity of an EGU due to system/equipment modification or discounting a portion of capacity for planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derates may affect base load rating, nameplate capacity, and capacity-factor calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Fossil fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Fossil fuel means natural gas, petroleum, coal, and any solid/liquid/gaseous fuel derived from such material for creating useful heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition scopes applicability for 'fossil fuel-fired' unit classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Gross energy output (three cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross energy output means: (1) for turbines/IGCC, gross electric or mechanical output plus 100% of useful thermal output; (2) for steam generating units, gross electric/mechanical output minus electricity used to power feedwater pumps plus 100% useful thermal output; (3) for CHP facilities meeting the 20.0% useful thermal output threshold, a specific adjustment dividing net electric output difference by 0.95 plus 100% useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the correct case based on unit type and CHP threshold; feedwater pump auxiliary load treatment differs for IGCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Heat recovery steam generating unit (HRSG)
rubrics_metrics.description: HRSG means a unit in which hot exhaust gases from a combustion turbine are routed to extract heat and generate useful output; HRSGs can be used with or without duct burners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify HRSGs when accounting for combined-cycle or duct-burner contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Integrated gasification combined cycle (IGCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: IGCC means a combined cycle facility designed to burn fuels containing ≥50% (by heat input) solid-derived fuel not meeting natural gas definition plus any integrated equipment providing electricity/useful thermal output; Administrator may waive 50% during construction/startup/shutdown/repair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IGCC classification affects fuel and output accounting; waivers possible during certain periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: ISO conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: ISO conditions means 288 Kelvin (15 °C), 60% relative humidity, and 101.3 kPa pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ISO conditions when referencing base load rating determinations and certain conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Mechanical output conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical output means useful mechanical energy not used to operate the facility, generate electricity/thermal output, or enhance performance; horsepower-hour must be converted to MWh by multiplying by 745.7 and dividing by 1,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply conversion factor precisely when incorporating mechanical output into MWh accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Nameplate capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nameplate capacity means, from initial installation, the maximum electrical generating output a generator/machine is capable of producing (in MWe, rounded to nearest tenth) on a steady-state basis as specified by manufacturer or after physical change increasing maximum output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use manufacturer-specified steady-state maximums; update after physical changes with documented basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Natural gas
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas means a fluid mixture of hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethane, propane) composed of at least 70% methane by volume or with gross calorific value between 35 and 41 MJ per dry standard cubic meter; excludes landfill/digester/refinery/sour/blast furnace/coal-derived/producer/coke oven gas or any gaseous fuel with highly variable CO2 content or heating value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fuel classification affects unit type definitions (natural gas-fired vs coal-fired etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural gas-fired steam generating unit means an electric utility steam generating unit that is fossil fuel-fired, is not a coal-fired or oil-fired unit, no longer retains capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029, and burns natural gas for >10.0% of average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or >15.0% during any one calendar year after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification depends on fuel fractions and capability to fire coal post-2029.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net electric output
rubrics_metrics.description: Net electric output means gross generation measured at generator terminals less electricity used to operate the plant (auxiliary loads such as fuel handling, pumps, fans, pollution control equipment, transformer losses measured at transmission side of step-up transformer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generator terminal measurements minus auxiliary loads to compute net electric output for P_gross/net calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Net energy output
rubrics_metrics.description: Net energy output means (1) net electric/mechanical output plus 100% useful thermal output measured relative to SATP that is not used to generate additional electric/mechanical output or enhance performance; (2) for CHP facilities meeting the 20% thresholds for both electric and thermal output on a 12-month rolling basis, the net electric/mechanical output divided by 0.95 plus 100% useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply SATP conditions for thermal output and CHP 0.95 adjustment when thresholds met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Oil-fired steam generating unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Oil-fired steam generating unit means an electric utility steam generating unit that is fossil fuel-fired, not coal-fired, not retaining capability to fire coal after Dec 31, 2029, and burns oil for >10.0% of average annual heat input during any continuous 3-calendar-year period after Dec 31, 2029, or >15.0% during any one calendar year after Dec 31, 2029.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fuel-share thresholds determine oil-fired classification for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP)
rubrics_metrics.description: SATP means 298.15 Kelvin (25 °C) and 100.0 kilopascals pressure. The enthalpy of water at SATP conditions is 50 Btu/lb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SATP for enthalpy and thermal output calculations where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: State agent
rubrics_metrics.description: State agent means an entity acting on behalf of the State, with the legal authority of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State agents may perform actions delegated by the State within their legal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Stationary combustion turbine (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stationary combustion turbine includes all equipment such as turbine engine, fuel/air/lubrication/exhaust systems, control systems (except emissions control equipment), heat recovery, fuel compressor/heater/pump, post-combustion emission control tech, ancillary components for simple-cycle, combined-cycle, and CHP turbine-based systems plus any integrated equipment that provides electricity or useful thermal output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the full turbine system including integrated equipment as part of the stationary combustion turbine definition for applicability and monitoring.
